To connect to this server, use the Private Endpoint from inside your virtual network'; error 42101 'Unable to create or modify firewall rules when public network interface for the server is disabled'; changes take effect immediately. That a client resolves the private endpoint's address only if the privatelink.database.windows.net private DNS zone is linked to its virtual network is from memory of the Private Link DNS guidance (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the database administrator at Haldane Freight, a fictional logistics firm. Last night security set 'Public network access' to Disable on the logical server sql-fin; the finance app reaches it through a private endpoint in vnet-app. The reporting server rpt-vm01, in vnet-reporting (peered with vnet-app), refreshes the board pack from sql-fin at 07:00. Its 05:30 test refresh failed.
handover: The private endpoint pe-sql-fin is in vnet-app; the private DNS zone privatelink.database.windows.net was created with it.
Security's change ticket: public access stays disabled; no exceptions.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the server's public and private endpoints, the private DNS zone and which networks it is linked to.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the refresh failed after public access was disabled, what you changed, and why not reopen the public endpoint.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: With public access disabled only private endpoint connections are allowed. rpt-vm01 resolved sql-fin to its public address because the privatelink zone was linked only to vnet-app, so it hit the closed public endpoint.

parts.label: Change
parts.modelAnswer: Linked the private DNS zone to vnet-reporting; the name now resolves to 10.10.4.5 and the connection goes over the peering. A firewall rule cannot even be created with public access disabled (error 42101).

parts.label: Not public
parts.modelAnswer: Re-enabling public access with an allow-all rule would have exposed the finance database to the internet against the agreed change. The link is now in code with a check.

exposed.headline: The private path was there all along
exposed.body: The endpoint and the peering worked; only DNS was wrong. Link the private DNS zone to the client's network instead of reopening the public endpoint.

packStale.headline: Private Link needs private DNS
packStale.body: With public access disabled, a client must reach the private endpoint, and it only does if its network resolves the name through the linked privatelink zone.

private.headline: Good: fixed resolution, kept the control
private.body: You saw the client resolve the public address, found the zone linked only to the app network, linked it to the reporting network, checked the query, and put a link check in the pipeline.

scoring.modelReasoning: Error 47073 means the client reached the public endpoint, which is disabled. The private endpoint is reachable over the peering, but rpt-vm01 resolves the public address because the privatelink zone is linked only to vnet-app. Link the zone to vnet-reporting and the name resolves privately. Firewall rules belong to the disabled public endpoint and cannot be created; reopening public access exposes the database. Put the link in code and check consumers.
